source.title: Some of my favorite open problems

accepted.question_text: Consider the discrete d-dimensional torus Z_N^d, and replace each undirected edge by two directed edges so that every vertex has in-degree equal to out-degree equal to 2d. In this balanced directed graph, any Eulerian circuit determines 2d directed loops based at the origin. For fixed dimension d >= 3, prove that for a uniform random Eulerian circuit, some of these 2d loops have length O(1) while all of the others have length of order N^d as N -> infinity.
accepted.context_brief: Random Eulerian circuits on the discrete torus

evidence.quote: Now as a simple example consider the discrete torus Z^d_N . Replace each edge by 2 directed edges. So in-degree = out-degree = 2d. Any Eulerian circuit consists of 2d “loops” from the origin.
Open problem. Prove (in fixed d ≥ 3) that of the 2d loops at the origin, some have length O(1), all others have length of order N d as N → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Choose k >= 2 distinct seed points z_1, ..., z_k in the unit square and assign seed z_i color i. Then sample independent uniformly distributed points U_{k+1}, U_{k+2}, ... in the unit square, and color each new point U_j with the color of the closest earlier point among U_1, ..., U_{j-1}, where U_i = z_i for 1 <= i <= k. Simulations suggest that as n -> infinity this procedure converges to a random partition of the square into k colored regions and that the boundaries between regions have zero area. Determine whether the boundary of this limit partition has fractal dimension exactly 1 or strictly greater than 1.
accepted.context_brief: Boundary geometry of a random coloring partition

evidence.quote: Choose k ≥ 2 distinct points z1 , . . . , zk in the unit square, and assign to point zi the color i from a palette of k colors. Take i.i.d. uniform random points Uk+1 , Uk+2 , . . . in the unit square, and inductively, for j ≥ k + 1, give point Uj the color of the closest point to Uj amongst U1 , . . . , Uj−1 where we interpret Ui = zi , 1 ≤ i ≤ k .
Aldous (2018) proves (by different methods) that the limit random partition exists in a certain weak sense. With Preater (2009) it follows that the boundaries have zero area.
Open problem. Does the boundary have fractal dimension = 1 or > 1 ?

accepted.question_text: Consider models of randomly coalescing partitions of the plane. In the specific time-reversed model described in the source, each country is absorbed at rate 1 per unit time, and when absorption occurs it is absorbed by the country whose capital city is closest to its own capital city; that model has an exact self-similarity property. For other models of randomly coalescing partitions of the plane, can any model be analyzed rigorously? More specifically, can one prove that such a model exhibits either asymptotic self-similarity or the appearance of a single infinite country, as in bond percolation theory?
accepted.context_brief: Other randomly coalescing planar partition models

evidence.quote: Each country is liable to be absorbed at rate 1 per unit time; if so it is absorbed by the country whose capital city is closest to its capital city.
From the explicit construction, this process automatically has an exact self-similarity property (from self-similarity of the space-time Poisson process).

Open problem. For other models of randomly coalescing partitions of the plane, we expect either asymptotic self-similarity or appearance of one infinite country (as in bond percolation theory). Can any other model be analyzed? [The Math Rule of 3].

accepted.question_text: Define the Lake Wobegon process as follows. Values arrive independently from a continuous distribution, and piles are kept in increasing order of their current pile averages from left to right. Each incoming value is placed on top of the first pile whose current average is higher than that value; if no such pile exists, a new pile is started at the right end. In the journal interpretation from the source, papers have independent Uniform[0,1] quality values with 0 representing the best quality, each journal accepts only papers whose quality is greater than the average quality of its previous accepted papers, and authors submit to the most prestigious journal that will accept the paper. Let X_n denote the journal sizes after n papers. Describe the limiting behavior of the distribution of X_n as n -> infinity.
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotics of the Lake Wobegon process

evidence.quote: So let us invent the Lake Wobegon process which is a variant of the patience sorting process. At any time the average of each pile is visible, and these averages are in increasing order of the piles. So the rule for placing the current card is place on top of the first (leftmost) pile whose average value is higher than the current card and if there is no such pile then start a new pile at the right end.

Submitted papers have a quality, uniform random on [0, 1], with 0 the best quality. Each journal only accepts papers whose quality is greater than the average of their previous accepted papers So the journals are ranked as 1st, 2nd, 3rd, . . . in decreasing order of prestige; authors then arrange to publish in the most prestigious journal that will accept.
Xn = journal sizes after n papers.
Open problem. Describe the limiting behavior of the distribution of Xn as n → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Suppose a sequence of symmetric finite Markov chains, after suitable time-scaling, converges to a limit Markov process that is represented measure-theoretically on ([0,1], Leb) by measurable transition kernels p_infinity(x,y,t) that are symmetric in x and y, have y -> p_infinity(x,y,t) as a probability density function for each x and t, and satisfy the Chapman-Kolmogorov relation. Can one recover from this limit analytic description the intrinsic topology of the natural state space of the limit process, rather than only a measure-theoretic realization on [0,1]?
accepted.context_brief: Recovering topology from a limit Markov kernel

evidence.quote: The n → ∞ limit processes we study will typically have continuous state space and continuous time 0 ≤ t < ∞. Working measure-theoretically we can take state space and stationary distribution to be ([0, 1], Leb).

Consider measurable functions p ∞ (x, y , t) for x, y ∈ [0, 1] and t > 0 such that p ∞ (x, y , t) ≡ p ∞ (y , x, t). y → p ∞ (x, y , t) is a probability density function. p ∞ (x, z, t + s) = p ∞ (x, y , t)p ∞ (y , z, s)dy . (Chapman-Kolmogorov)
Our intuition is that any “natural” sequence of Markov chains will have some “natural” limit process on some nice topological space.
So can we recover this topology from the limit analytic description?

accepted.question_text: For a limit symmetric Markov process described on [0,1] by transition kernels p_infinity(x,y,t), does there exist a natural metric on the state space, for example d(x_1,x_2) := sqrt(integral integral (p_infinity(x_1,y,t) - p_infinity(x_2,y,t))^2 e^{-t} dy dt), such that [0,1] becomes a complete separable metric space and the Markov process has the Feller property?
accepted.context_brief: Feller metric for a limit Markov process

evidence.quote: This specifies the finite-dimensional distributions of a symmetric Markov process on [0, 1] started at x.

Conjecture. There is some natural way to define a metric, for instance d(x_1,x_2) := sqrt(∫∫ (p_∞(x_1,y,t) − p_∞(x_2,y,t))^2 e^(−t) dy dt) which makes [0, 1] into a complete separable metric space and makes the Markov process have the Feller property.
